findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
Endpoints entered without a scheme default to cleartext http://. The network security config only allows cleartext for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and 10.0.2.2, so LAN endpoints will fail or users will be pushed to cleartext.
app/src/main/java/com/opendroid/ai/core/util/UrlUtils.kt:36: Defaults to http:// when no scheme is given.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
Cleartext is blocked by default but permitted for some domains. Check that nothing sensitive goes to them.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:8: cleartext permitted: localhost
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:9: cleartext permitted: 127.0.0.1
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:10: cleartext permitted: 10.0.2.2

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0242: Missing Certificate Pinning in Network Security Configuration
findings.explanation:
No pin-set in a network security config. Pinning may be done in code (OkHttp CertificatePinner, a custom TrustManager), which Ward doesn't read. MASVS L2 expects pinning; L1 doesn't.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:71: networkSecurityConfig @xml/network_security_config

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0224: Usage of Insecure APK Signature Version
findings.explanation:
The release signing config enables the v1 (JAR) signature scheme. With minSdk 26 v2+ is always available, and v1 leaves the app open to signature-stripping on older devices.
app/build.gradle:53: enableV1Signing is true in the release signing config.
